faqs.question: Will we definitely see gelada baboons?
faqs.answer: Gelada baboons are wild animals and sightings cannot be guaranteed. However, they are commonly seen in the gorge area, especially in the morning. Our guides know their usual haunts and will do their best to spot them.

faqs.question: Is the monastery still active?
faqs.answer: Yes, Debre Libanos is still an active monastery with resident monks. Visitors should dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered) and speak respectfully.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit?
faqs.answer: October to March (dry season) offers the clearest views and best wildlife spotting. The gorge is particularly dramatic after the rainy season (September–October).

faqs.question: What makes Tiya a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faqs.answer: Tiya contains 32 carved stone stelae dating to the 11th–13th centuries, featuring enigmatic symbols and decorations. It's one of the most important archaeological sites in Ethiopia, designated UNESCO World Heritage in 1980.

faqs.question: Is the Adadi Mariam church similar to Lalibela?
faqs.answer: Yes, Adadi Mariam is a rock-hewn church built during the same period as the Lalibela churches (13th century). While smaller, it features similar architectural techniques and religious significance.

faqs.question: What will I see at Melka Kunture?
faqs.answer: Melka Kunture is a Paleolithic archaeological site with stone tools, fossils, and an open-air museum. You'll see excavation areas where archaeologists have discovered tools dating back over 1 million years.
